content:
The image shows:
- Dense, fluffy white cottony mycelium covering the stem/crown area at or near the soil line
- Small, round, yellowish-tan sclerotia (mustard seed-sized, ~1-2mm) scattered throughout the mycelium
- Brown, rotted stem tissue underneath

Key diagnostic features:
- The small, spherical, tan sclerotia are the hallmark of *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight)
- Sclerotinia Timber Rot also has white mycelium but produces large, irregular black sclerotia — not small tan round ones
- The cottony growth at the crown/stem base with these characteristic mustard-seed sclerotia is textbook Southern Blight
